name: issue_821_scenario_e_sustain_confirmation_noise_rejection
description: Scenario E from the Issue #821 plan (rewritten post-#959, PROACTIVE_FLOOR removal): a direct reproduction of the physical pattern behind the live 300-second-gap finding (Zone 1's real WHF, 2026-08-31 13:06:46-13:30:00Z) -- a nat-vent session's exit candidate flickers true/false as outdoor temperature noisily crosses an exit threshold, rather than holding continuously. Asserts that with sustain-confirmation (NAT_VENT_EXIT_SUSTAIN_S=90s), a momentary, non-sustained crossing does NOT commit an exit -- the session survives two separate flickers of the exit condition, neither of which is ever held continuously for the full 90s window. Originally used PROACTIVE_FLOOR (the ODE time-to-floor prediction) as the flickering vehicle; that mechanism was fully removed by Issue #959, so this rewrite uses CEILING_THRESHOLD instead (outdoor rising above comfort_cool+nat_vent_delta) -- still one of the 4 non-exempt exit reasons gated by the identical, generic _confirm_nat_vent_exit_candidate() sustain clock, so the mechanism under test (sustain-confirmation itself) is unchanged; only the physical trigger used to flicker it is different.
source: Issue #821 plan, Design's required 'Golden/pending scenario E' -- Verification BLOCKING #2. Rewritten for Issue #959 (PROACTIVE_FLOOR removal).
notes: Issue #959 disposition: indoor is held at a constant 80F throughout (rather than drifting, as the original PROACTIVE_FLOOR version needed) because CEILING_THRESHOLD's trigger is purely an outdoor-temperature threshold crossing (outdoor > comfort_cool + nat_vent_delta = 74+3 = 77F) -- no thermal-model-driven prediction is involved, so no k_passive/thermal_model is needed at all (omitted; confidence defaults to 'none', which also keeps handle_door_window_open's unrelated thermal-model floor-imminence pre-activation guard out of play).

Priority-order constraint (nat_vent_exit.py's decide_nat_vent_exit(), checked in order: MANUAL_OVERRIDE_CONFLICT, COMFORT_FLOOR, AWAY_CEILING, OUTDOOR_RISE, CEILING_THRESHOLD): OUTDOOR_RISE is checked BEFORE CEILING_THRESHOLD and fires on outdoor >= indoor (non-strict, Issue #690). To isolate CEILING_THRESHOLD specifically (not accidentally trip OUTDOOR_RISE instead), indoor is kept at 80F -- comfortably above the 77F ceiling threshold outdoor flickers around, so outdoor(78) < indoor(80) throughout and OUTDOOR_RISE never fires. COMFORT_FLOOR also never fires (indoor 80F is far above the 68F daytime floor).

Honesty note (same standard as the original scenario's own Q9 caveat): this reproduces the PHYSICAL PATTERN (an exit candidate flickering on/off around its threshold, never sustained) using a different, still-live mechanism than the original live incident traced to -- it is not a byte-exact replay of the original PROACTIVE_FLOOR-based reproduction, which is no longer possible now that mechanism is deleted. The pattern (arm at t, clear at t+30s, re-arm fresh at t+305s, still unconfirmed at t+45s-into-the-second-arm) is preserved exactly.

Companion negative control: tests/test_scenario_e_sustain_confirmation_negative_control.py loads this exact JSON and re-runs it twice -- once normally (confirming the session survives, matching this file's own assertions) and once with _confirm_nat_vent_exit_candidate() patched to commit immediately (bypassing sustain-confirmation entirely), confirming THAT run's session does NOT survive the very first flicker at 08:10:00. That second run is the negative control the Issue #821 plan's Design required -- it cannot be expressed inside this JSON scenario format alone, since JSON scenarios have no mechanism to monkeypatch production code; see that test file for the actual revert-tested proof.

Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec.10): (a) Scenario effectiveness: this scenario's own assertion (nat_vent_still_active at 08:16:20) would FAIL if sustain-confirmation were removed -- proven directly by the companion negative-control test file, not just asserted here. (b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md Sec.6f should be updated to note NAT_VENT_EXIT_SUSTAIN_S's test reference switched from a PROACTIVE_FLOOR-based scenario to this CEILING_THRESHOLD-based one after Issue #959. (c) Occupant experience: without sustain-confirmation, a single noisy outdoor reading crossing an exit threshold ends free cooling and restores active HVAC, even though the underlying trend never actually called for it -- costing the occupant real energy and comfort disruption for no real benefit. With sustain-confirmation, the session correctly rides out momentary noise and only ends when the condition genuinely holds.

events.note: Hot-day classification, HVAC in cool mode.
Baseline: indoor 80F, outdoor 65F -- favorable for nat-vent, well below the 77F ceiling threshold (comfort_cool 74 + nat_vent_delta 3).
Window opens: outdoor(65) < indoor(80), indoor > comfort_heat(68), outdoor < threshold(77) -- nat-vent activates, WHF turns on.

First flicker: outdoor rises to 78F, above the 77F ceiling threshold. CEILING_THRESHOLD candidate arms via decide_nat_vent_exit() (outdoor(78) < indoor(80), so OUTDOOR_RISE does not fire first) -- NOT yet sustain-confirmed (Issue #821, NAT_VENT_EXIT_SUSTAIN_S=90s). Session still active this tick.

30s later (< 90s sustain window) -- outdoor recovers to 76F, below the 77F threshold. decide_nat_vent_exit() returns NONE this tick, resetting the candidate's timer entirely (confirmed_transition.py's own documented reset-on-clear behavior) -- the CEILING_THRESHOLD condition clears before ever being sustained for 90s.

305s after the first flicker (well past the unrelated 300s fan-toggle rate-limit window, and well past the 30s recovery above) -- outdoor rises back to 78F, the SAME CEILING_THRESHOLD condition arms again, but as a genuinely FRESH candidate (the previous one was cleared at 08:10:30, not carried over) -- not yet sustain-confirmed (elapsed 0s). Session still active this tick.

45s after the second flicker's fresh arm (< 90s NAT_VENT_EXIT_SUSTAIN_S) -- still not confirmed. Session must still be active at this point: with sustain-confirmation, NEITHER flicker (30s continuous, then 45s-and-counting continuous) ever reached the full 90s of continuous above-threshold reading required to commit.

assertions.reason: Nat-vent activates on window-open per the standard 4-condition gate.

Two separate flickers of the CEILING_THRESHOLD exit condition (30s and 45s-and-counting) never individually held continuously for the full 90s NAT_VENT_EXIT_SUSTAIN_S window required to commit -- the session correctly survives noise that would have caused an instantaneous-commit design (pre-Issue #821) to exit and restore HVAC unnecessarily. See tests/test_scenario_e_sustain_confirmation_negative_control.py for the revert-tested proof that this assertion genuinely depends on sustain-confirmation being present.

verdict.summary: A nat-vent session survives repeated momentary (noisy) crossings of the CEILING_THRESHOLD exit condition, exiting only when the condition is genuinely sustained -- reproducing the physical pattern behind the live 300-second-gap finding and proving sustain-confirmation actually prevents it, via a still-existing exit reason now that PROACTIVE_FLOOR (the original vehicle) has been removed (Issue #959).
verdict.observed_behavior: CEILING_THRESHOLD candidate arms at 08:10:00, clears at 08:10:30 (recovered before 90s), re-arms fresh at 08:15:35, still unconfirmed at 08:16:20 (45s < 90s) -- nat-vent remains active throughout.
verdict.expected_behavior: Momentary/noisy readings crossing an exit threshold must not, by themselves, end a nat-vent session -- only a condition that holds continuously for the full sustain window should commit, directly addressing the reported real-world flapping.
